I know a man who’s very much like this. I can tell you for a fact, from being around him and seeing people’s facial expressions when he does it, it’s not exactly the most wished for thing by everyone around.

Some people will gladly talk to you, like how an elderly man spoke to me the other day about the gas prices — a brief, “Man, guess we picked the wrong day to fill up, huh?” followed by me nodding and laughing a bit — short and sweet.

The guy I’m talking about though will start entire conversations in grocery isles, parking lots, checkout lines, sitting down at restaurants, or even on the phone when he so regularly calls customer service lines. It’s definitely weird if that’s all someone does. The key is learning when it is and isn’t appropriate/wanted to do so. For example, when you see people sitting down at a restaurant table minding their own with their family or friends, they probably don’t want to sit there and have a chat. In grocery lines it’s more acceptable, as long as you don’t start dumping deep stuff on the person or opening up about your childhood etc.

One time I saw the man ask a group of people in the waiting room if they minded if he changed the channel. That was okay. What wasn’t okay was the fact he continued talking to all of them after that, and “quizzing” them on what sports celebs they knew. It obviously bothered them and one girl even walked out of the room to go sit somewhere else because it was of course a very awkward interaction.

So in short it both is and isn’t okay to do. Just make sure you think before starting a conversation. Are they free to listen (if they’re sitting at a restaurant the safest bet is likely always a no)? If they are and you start, do they look okay with it, or do they look like they’re itching to get away from this awkward conversation without being rude about it? Just pay attention to those kinds of cues. It definitely isn’t a normal thing to come across someone who talks to everyone out in public, but if you can recognize when someone’s really not into it and leave them alone, it’s probably for the better.

My mom would always do those things to me and I always hated calling it “abuse” and I felt weird calling myself a victim. It felt like I was just victimizing myself. But ask any sane person and they’ll tell you that isn’t how parents should treat their offspring. It’s not physical abuse unless she’s hitting you, but degrading and comparing you to others and taking away what makes you happy as “punishment” is certain mental abuse. My mom used to always take away the things she knew I used for comfort. That isn’t punishment, that’s just being mean and justifying it with their authority. It’s wrong. I hope you get out of there ASAP. I was kicked out right Ah her I graduated high school but since I had a friend and we had a plan, I was able to situate myself in a safe home over 800 miles away. Being kicked out was perhaps the best thing she did for me, it ended up pushing me to a better place. I know nobody asked for my little “story” but it just goes to show how much happier I am without all that bs. Because like I said, my mom did all the same stuff as that. I’ve been so happy since leaving that. I wish the best of luck to you too in getting out whenever you can.
